test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II Official Paper-I (Held On: 20 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

Through the dense forest, / the hikers / trekked / for hours / before reaching / the mountain peak.

options.text: Through the dense forest for hours trekked the hikers before reaching the mountain peak.
The hikers trekked for hours through the dense forest before reaching the mountain peak.
Before reaching the mountain peak, the hikers through the dense forest trekked for hours.
The hikers for hours through the dense forest trekked before reaching the mountain peak.

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. The hikers trekked for hours through the dense forest before reaching the mountain peak. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This sentence describes a sequence of actions that the hikers undertook.
 
• The order of the clauses logically follows the chronology of the actions.
 
• The subject of the sentence "the hikers" should be followed by the main verb "trekked".
 
• The phrase "for hours" indicates the duration of the action and follows directly after the verb 'trekked'.
 
• The prepositional phrase "through the dense forest" shows where the action took place and modifies the verb.
 
• Finally, the infinitive phrase "before reaching the mountain peak" shows the concluding action after the hike.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The placement of adverbial phrases (like "for hours" and "through the dense forest") is important for clarity and flow.
 
• The structure used in the correct sentence typically follows the pattern: Subject + Main Verb + Additional information describing the action (such as adverbials of time, place, or manner).
 
• In English, the placement of time-related information generally comes after the verb or at the end of the sentence.
 
• Understanding the role and typical placement of these sentence components can help construct clear, coherent sentences.
